« Écrire et rapper, c’est une forme de r: “Writing and rapping is a form of resistance”
Si la scène hip-hop montréalaise n’a ces: While Montréal’s hip-hop scene has kept growing over the years, women’s place in it has only begun to take on real weight over the past decade or so. Pioneers of local and national rap have paved the way for emerging artists like SteinZ and Guessmi, but according to the women themselves, there is still a lot to be done.
<strong>Être une rappeuse dans un monde: Being a female rapper in a man’s world: Guessmi’s story
Si on traverse l’un des ponts dans le no: Cross one of the bridges in northern Montréal and you land in Laval, a city that has vanished from the postcards. A municipality that at times concentrates the same social inequalities as Montréal-Nord: higher unemployment than the provincial average and more precarity, among other things. Laval’s hip-hop scene is therefore often associated with that of its neighbouring city, with some artists depicting similar issues there.
Guessmi est une jeune rappeuse lavallois: Guessmi is a young rapper from Laval of Tunisian origin. She is 23 years old and was born and raised in Quebec. Having attended a Muslim school for most of her schooling, she says she “wasn’t mixed in with the other (cultures) of Montréal.” It is only since entering adulthood that she has been immersed in Montréal’s melting pot.
Pour Guessmi, c’est une évidence : d’aus: For Guessmi, it’s obvious: for as long as she can remember, singing and rapping have helped her feel better. “In the beginning, I wrote lyrics in my room. It was very personal. I didn’t let anyone see them, not even my friends; I was too shy,” she recalls, with a timid half-smile. “Then one day, I ended up in a recording studio by chance, going along with a friend. I picked up a mic and gave it a try. I was surprised by the result; on my way home, I knew I had to do something with it.”
Les textes de l’artiste lavalloise trait: The Laval artist’s lyrics draw heavily on her personal experiences. “For me, my music is a way of telling myself that even when things are going badly, life goes on and the tide turns,” she sums up.
La séparation de ses parents alors qu’el: Her parents’ separation when she was very young, and adjusting to life in a single-parent household, left a mark on her. Writing has therefore become more than a pastime for Guessmi; it has become a necessity.
« Quand on est une femme dans un monde d: “When you’re a woman in a man’s world, everyday life is hard,” the artist begins. Brow furrowed, she pauses to think, seems to call up certain memories, then continues. “Every day is a fight. I know I shouldn’t play the victim or focus on that, but it’s the reality.” In an arena dominated mostly by men, being a female rapper is a big challenge, but, she says, never to the point of making her doubt her career. “I don’t want to be associated with something I’m not. I just want to have a place that’s respected, the same as if I were a man, because if I were a man, I know I wouldn’t be facing the same reality,” she goes on, before adding: “When I suggest ideas, when I ask for advice, even when I speak, sometimes I’m not taken seriously.”
Guessmi ne mâche pas ses mots pour dénon: Guessmi does not mince words in denouncing the sexism that runs through the profession. “It’s not limited to artists. There are almost no women in the industry at all. Videographers, producers, publicists, photographers, journalists, and so on. When I meet a woman in the same industry as me, I automatically think we have to stick together, because we’re living the same negative realities,” she adds.
En tant qu’artiste hip-hop, Guessmi s’in: As a hip-hop artist, Guessmi is worried about the significant place rape culture holds in her industry. “We’ve normalized so many sexist and problematic lyrics in hip-hop. It’s everywhere now,” she exclaims. “Since it’s mainly men who take part in producing those tracks, it’s easy to trivialize a reality they don’t experience.” Visibly frustrated, she rolls her eyes before continuing: “I even see women trivialize lyrics that degrade women and don’t respect them. I don’t understand. It’s so ingrained in our heads, and it’s very serious. Young people are going to grow up surrounded by this kind of message and won’t see the problem when a sexist incident, or worse, happens in front of them. If statements like that are considered normal, we shouldn’t be surprised by all the problems that come with them,” she says indignantly.
Dans une optique plus positive, la rappe: On a more positive note, the rapper says the issue is being taken more and more seriously. She cites as an example a track by French rapper Tayc: Quand tu dors. Accused of romanticizing a non-consensual sexual encounter, it was pulled from streaming platforms last spring. “Mentalities are changing, the music world is evolving. It’s still not what we’d like it to be, but it’s getting better, and that’s better than nothing,” she says happily.
L’une des solutions au sexisme dans le r: For her, one of the solutions to sexism in rap lies in giving back to her community. “If I know one person is listening to me and feels better for it, that matters more than a thousand others listening and feeling nothing. I know how hard it is to be young in Montréal and the surrounding area, even more so if you’re a woman – and even more so if you’re racialized. I want young people, when they see me, to see hope, and to have fun with my music!” the artist concludes, her smile back on her face.
<strong>Le rap pour s’exprimer, le cas d: Rap as self-expression: the case of SteinZ
Issue du quartier Saint-Laurent, SteinZ: From the Saint-Laurent borough, SteinZ was born to a Haitian mother and a Gambian father. Gradually carving out a path in Montréal’s hip-hop industry, this sci-fi and horror fan draws her stage name from Frankenstein, author R.L. Stine and Albert Einstein, a figure who fascinates her.
Si SteinZ s’est lancée dans le monde du: SteinZ got into rap so that a wide audience could see themselves in her story. “I was always looking for a more ‘official’ way to express myself, to share my life in a way that could have an impact,” she says.
Ses influences, ce sont principalement d: Her influences are mainly two American rappers. “First Doja Cat, because she helped me discover the alternative kind of rap I do. She’s an idol to me. You can even hear a little bit of Doja Cat in my style,” she explains, smiling. “She inspired me a lot. It was listening to her that made me wonder if I could do something similar. She stayed authentic, even though a lot of people criticized her.” Another idol: “Nicki Minaj, a pioneer of women’s rap, obviously. She’s one of the first of our generation who managed to get a seat at the same table as the male rappers.” According to SteinZ, Minaj influenced her “unconsciously,” because she has listened to her since a young age and absorbed her musical presence.
Sur une note plus personnelle, la jeune: On a more personal note, the young rapper says the people around her are also one of her great sources of inspiration. “For a long time, I’ve followed a simple approach: ‘Always surround yourself with people who have a talent similar to mine and who are succeeding.’ It’s a thought that can seem a bit negative, but I’ve learned that’s how you motivate yourself to reach your destination.” SteinZ made this maxim her own by spending time at <l1>Studio NBS (NotBadSound)</l1>. It was also in this community space that she got a foot in the door of Montréal’s music industry, and where she met her mentor, Jai Nitai. At the studio that, in a way, saw her born as an artist, she says the saying takes on its full meaning.
« Un problème qui me tient à cœur, c’est: “One issue that’s close to my heart is broken families. Especially families that suffer from the father’s absence,” she begins. “If you look at the statistics, families where the father is absent make up about 25% of the white population. For Hispanic families, that number goes up to 50, 52%. And for Black families, it reaches 72%”*, she explains. “It’s absolutely ridiculous. Of course there are historical factors that play an important role in all of this,” she continues.
Avec le rap comme exutoire, elle espère,: With rap as an outlet, she hopes, she says, to “break this toxic cycle.” To change things, SteinZ believes that “not losing hope and continuing to move forward, even when times seem hard” helps in facing the consequences of single parenthood. “The way I see the world, it’s like a game of cards. Even if I’ve got the worst cards in my hand, the game isn’t over. It’s over when I decide it is, and I’m not going to give up. There’s always a way to play your cards well, and that’s what I want to do.”
« Écrire et rapper, c’est une forme de r: “Writing and rapping is a form of resistance,” the artist concludes.
Les récits de SteinZ et de Guessmi diffè: SteinZ’s and Guessmi’s stories differ in how they confront the problems that affect them. Yet they come together in their desire to gradually revolutionize their industry. While the personal struggles of these two women sit at the heart of the lyrics in their performances, in both cases it is a form of resistance.
